### CLAUDE (2026-07-17T19:12:22.053Z)

Valid and coherent. Here's how to go from your CSVs to a route-optimization input.

## The two CSVs are the plan; the optimization input is a JSON

- `territories.csv` — the summary (rep → channel, customer count, per-weekday loads).
- `pos_assignments.csv` — the operative one: every POS → its rep and its visit days.

You have two ways to turn that into an optimization input:

### Option A — reproduce it (deterministic)
The assignment is deterministic (same `--input`/`--target-per-rep`/`--seed`), so just add `--fixed-input` to your original command:
```bash
.venv/bin/python rolling_horizon_territories.py --input jim_original_input.json \
  --target-per-rep 80 --out-dir territory_out2 --fixed-input
```
It re-derives the identical plan and writes `territory_out2/input_territories.json`.

### Option B — build straight from the CSVs (new `--from-csv`)
I just added this so the CSVs are a usable, **editable** source of truth — review or adjust `pos_assignments.csv`, then:
```bash
.venv/bin/python rolling_horizon_territories.py --input jim_original_input.json \
  --out-dir territory_out2 --from-csv
```
I already ran it for you → **`territory_out2/input_territories.json`**. Validated: 19,370 jobs each pinned to exactly one rep-zone and one single-day window; 1,660 vehicles (83 reps × 4 weeks × 5 days) with integer ids; all 83 zones served.

## Then optimize (per day / per week)
That single JSON holds all 4 weeks. Feed it to the existing pipeline — it decomposes into one shift per day and solves. For the first week:
```bash
D=$(pwd)
.venv/bin/python rolling_horizon.py --no-zones \
  --input "$D/territory_out2/input_territories.json" \
  --workdir "$D/territory_out2/sim_runs" \
  --simulator "$D/sim_runs/simulator" \
  --days 5 --limit-s 60
```
Use `--days 20` for all four weeks, or omit `--days` for everything. Then, as before, you can combine the day inputs (`combine_day_inputs.py`) or read KPIs from the `day_NN_output.json` files.

**One structural note:** it's not one optimization — it's **one shift per (rep-day)**, coupled only through the fixed territories (a vehicle's `allowed_zones` restricts it to its rep's POS) and the day-pinned windows. That's why a single input file yields a set of per-day solves rather than one giant problem.

### CLAUDE (2026-07-18T13:11:33.493Z)

Fixed and verified end-to-end.

## Root cause
The `SHARED_URL` links pointed at valid solutions, but `nb-share.ts` only called **`solutions:save`** — which *persists* a solution but leaves it `is_shared: false`. The `route-planner-viewer` page loads a solution through the **public `shared-solutions/{id}`** endpoint, which returns **404/403 until the solution is actually shared**. So every generated link was a dead end. (The token itself was fine — valid through 2026-07-28, not expired.)

## The fix
`saveSolution` now does two steps instead of one:
1. `POST solutions:save` — persist.
2. `POST solutions/{id}:share` — **mark it shared** (`is_shared → true`). This is the step that was missing.

I found `solutions/{id}:share` by probing the BFF (the console's "Share" button hits it; plain `solutions:share` without the id is a no-op, and `PATCH … {is_shared:true}` is silently ignored).

## Verified
- Before share: `shared-solutions/{id}` → **404**.
- After save+share: `shared-solutions/{id}` (no cookie) → **200**, returns the solution.
- **In a real browser, while logged out of the console**, the `route-planner-viewer` link rendered the route (PT_113, 71.56 km, 215 steps).
- Build clean.

## Two things to know
- **Existing exported links won't retroactively work** — they were saved-but-not-shared. Re-run **"Run all → Excel"** (it now shares each solution as it goes) and the new `SHARED_URL` values will resolve.
- **The share still depends on `NB_BFF_TOKEN`**, which expires **2026-07-28**. After that, the save/share calls 401 and the column goes blank again until you refresh the token in `.env.local` (and the Secret Manager secret, if deployed).

**WA 1 is full.** The map hardcodes `CAPS = [34000, 20000, 20000]`, and the legend shows WA 1 at **33,995 / 34,000 daily parcels = 100% utilization**. So even though WA 1 is nearest to `32-641` (340.2 km), it has essentially no room. Among the depots that *do* have spare capacity — WA 2 (71%) and WA 3 (75%) — WA 3 at **357.8 km is closer than WA 2 at 388.8 km**, so WA 3 is the best *feasible* choice. WA 1 isn't a "better option" here because it's not actually available.

**This is what the whole WA 1 / WA 3 boundary looks like.** WA 1 is saturated, so a band of codes that geographically belong to it must overflow into WA 3. You'll see this everywhere along that green line.

**And `32-641` is a *good* code to overflow, not a mistake.** Its penalty for using WA 3 instead of WA 1 is only 17.6 km, and it's tiny (0.1 parcels/day). A capacity-constrained optimizer minimizes total distance by spilling the *cheapest-to-move* codes first and reserving WA 1's scarce capacity for codes that would suffer a much bigger detour. Picking this one to overflow is exactly the right move.

## One caveat on auditing it further
The allocation itself was **precomputed by a generator that isn't in this repo** — `depot_allocation_map_6.html` is a self-contained *display* artifact (each postal code already carries its assigned depot plus the three distances for the tooltip; I checked, there's no assignment algorithm or source script here, only the render logic + baked data). So I can confirm the *cause* (WA 1 at capacity → cheapest overflows spill to the nearest depot with room), but I can't re-run or prove the exact set of overflow codes is globally min-cost without that generator.

If you want to change the outcome, the levers are: **raise WA 1's capacity** (34,000 is the binding constraint), **add/relocate a depot** to serve the WA1/WA3 seam, or if you suspect the overflow choices aren't optimal, share the generator script and I'll audit it. if [ -f .env.local ]; then
```bash
  TOKEN=$(grep -E '^NB_BFF_TOKEN=' .env.local | head -1 | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '"'"'"'')
  if [ -n "$TOKEN" ]; then
    echo "NB_BFF_TOKEN present in .env.local (length ${#TOKEN})"
    # Decode JWT exp claim to check expiry (payload is 2nd segment)
    PAYLOAD=$(echo "$TOKEN" | cut -d. -f2)
    # pad base64
    python3 - "$PAYLOAD" <<'PY'
import sys, base64, json, datetime
p = sys.argv[1] + "=" * (-len(sys.argv[1]) % 4)
try:
    d = json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(p))
    exp = d.get("exp")
    if exp:
        print("JWT exp:", datetime.datetime.utcfromtimestamp(exp).isoformat(), "UTC")
except Exception as e:
    print("could not decode exp:", e)
PY
  else
    echo "NB_BFF_TOKEN NOT found in .env.local"
  fi
else
  echo ".env.local not found"
fi
```

Fixed. The `NB_BFF_TOKEN` is now wired into the running Cloud Run revision (confirmed in the env list above), `shared_urls_enabled = true`, and the image is unchanged.

**Root cause:** The `SHARED_URL` column is populated by `/api/optimize/all`, which only generates a link when `process.env.NB_BFF_TOKEN` is set (`route.ts:83`). Locally that comes from `demo/.env.local`, but that file is deliberately excluded from the Docker image (secrets never get baked in). In terraform, the `nb_bff_token` line in `terraform.tfvars` was **commented out**, so `bff_enabled` was `false` — the secret and env var were never provisioned. The deployed app ran with `NB_BFF_TOKEN` undefined, so every `SHARED_URL` cell came back empty.

**What I changed:**
- Uncommented/set `nb_bff_token` in `terraform.tfvars` (git-ignored, secret never printed), sourced from `demo/.env.local`.
- `terraform apply` created the `dhl-pl-demo-nb-bff-token` Secret Manager secret, granted the run service account access, and rolled a new revision with the `NB_BFF_TOKEN` env var. Same image tag, so nothing else changed.

**Verified:** `NB_BFF_TOKEN` is present on the running revision; `shared_urls_enabled = true`. This is the same token that generated working shared links earlier in the session — the only thing missing was wiring it to Cloud Run.

**Two things to flag:**
1. **The token expires 2026-07-28** (8 days out). After that the `SHARED_URL` column will go empty again until you refresh the `ncc_token` JWT from a logged-in console session, update it in both `demo/.env.local` and `terraform.tfvars`, and re-apply.
2. Re-run **Run all → Excel** on the deployed site to get a fresh export — the `SHARED_URL` column should now be populated. Want me to trigger that run now to confirm live? ### CLAUDE (2026-07-20T22:39:26.617Z)

Fully diagnosed. Here's what's wrong and how I found it.

## Root cause

The running `glwas-demo` revision has its **entire env list replaced with just `REDEPLOYED_AT`** — the `NB_API_KEY` Secret Manager reference is gone. The container reads `process.env.NB_API_KEY` (`demo/src/app/api/optimize/route.ts:21`), gets `undefined`, and returns "NB_API_KEY not configured".

The secret material is fine — `glwas-demo-nb-api-key` exists with 3 enabled versions (latest 2026-07-15). Only the **wiring** on the deployed revision was lost.

**How it happened:** a manual `gcloud run deploy … --set-env-vars REDEPLOYED_AT=…` (or the Console) was used. `--set-env-vars` *replaces* the whole env list rather than merging, so it dropped the secret-backed `NB_API_KEY`. The `terraform plan` also shows it dropped the public-invoker IAM binding (`google_cloud_run_v2_service_iam_member.public` needs re-creating), which points to the same out-of-band deploy.

## The troubleshooting sequence (reusable)

```bash
SVC=glwas-demo; REGION=us-central1
# 1. Is the key even wired on the running revision?
gcloud run services describe $SVC --region $REGION \
  --format="json(spec.template.spec.containers[0].env)"      # ← showed only REDEPLOYED_AT
# 2. Does the secret still exist / have versions?
gcloud secrets versions list ${SVC}-nb-api-key
# 3. What does IaC think should be there? (read-only)
terraform plan -var image="<current-image>"                  # ← shows env being restored
```
If step 1 shows the secret ref present but calls still fail, it'd instead be a *bad key value* (rotate the secret + redeploy) or an NB-side 401/403 — different fix. Here it's a missing wiring.

## The fix

Re-apply terraform — it restores the full env (NB_API_KEY → secret `latest` = v3) and the public IAM binding, keeping the current image:

```bash
cd GLWAS/terraform
CUR_IMG=$(gcloud run services describe glwas-demo --region us-central1 \
  --format="value(spec.template.spec.containers[0].image)")
terraform apply -var image="$CUR_IMG"   # plan: 1 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy
```

Passing `-var image=` is essential — omitting it resets the service to the GCP hello-sample placeholder (the `image` default in `variables.tf`).

To avoid a recurrence, redeploy this service **only** through `terraform apply` (or, if using `gcloud run deploy`, use `--update-env-vars` not `--set-env-vars`, and never omit the secret).

Want me to run the `terraform apply` fix now? It's a prod change (in-place, ~15s, no image change), so I held off pending your go-ahead.

```bash
import json, datetime
TZ = datetime.timezone(datetime.timedelta(hours=-3))
inp = json.load(open("weekly_plan_out/week_1_input.json"))
jobs = {j["id"]: j for j in inp["jobs"]}

def audit(path, label):
    res = json.load(open(path))
    tot = late = 0
    worst = []
    for r in res["routes"]:
        for s in r["steps"]:
            if s["type"] != "job": continue
            tot += 1
            tws = jobs[s["id"]]["time_windows"]
            # late = arrival after the END of every window (no window can still be met)
            if all(s["arrival"] > tw[1] for tw in tws):
                late += 1
                worst.append((s["arrival"] - max(tw[1] for tw in tws), s["id"]))
    worst.sort(reverse=True)
    print(f"{label}: {tot} served, LATE beyond all windows: {late}")
    for lateness, jid in worst[:3]:
        print(f"    {jid}: {lateness/3600:.1f}h late")
audit("weekly_plan_out/week_1_solution.json", "layover run  ")
audit("weekly_plan_out/week_1_control_solution.json", "control run  ")
```

### CLAUDE (2026-07-21T15:05:44.066Z)

All 4 weeks solved cleanly. Here's the reset, complete and validated end-to-end.

## New approach: `weekly_layover_plan.py` (supersedes `rolling_horizon_territories.py`)

**Model:** one vehicle = one rep-week, shift spanning Mon 08:00 → Fri 15:30 (UTC-3). Per-day job windows (08:00–15:30 on each allowed weekday) partition the week into ≤7.5h daily segments with overnight waiting between them — 7.5h being the customer's own "Daily Time Available on Route" from the Obs sheet. The jobs landing on a rep-week vehicle **are** the rep's weekly territory, so territories fall directly out of rep assignment as you asked.

**Results (350 POS → 1,021 orders, seed 42):**
- **0 late arrivals, 0 unassigned** across all 4 weeks (~250–261 jobs/week, ~2,300 km/week).
- **No type mixing** — enforced via skills (one per TIPO DE VENDEDOR); every route audited pure.
- **TRAD reps work 4–5 days/week** at up to the 7.5h cap; AUTO/NOTU/FRAG reps work 2–4 days because their entire weekly workload is only 4–13h (a data property, not a solver failure).
- Frequencies honored: 2.0 → 2 visits/week split early/late week; 1.0 → weekly; 0.5 → weeks 1&3 or 2&4; 0.25 → one week; DIAS ATENDIMENTO / DIA RESTRIÇÃO respected via windows.
- Outputs in `weekly_plan_out/`: `week_N_input.json` + `week_N_solution.json`, `assignments.csv` (job → rep/date/arrival), `territories_summary.csv` (rep × week × per-day counts).

## The layover_config verdict — tested and rejected, with evidence

I built it exactly per your spec (27000s continuous / 43200s layover / include_service_time) and ran week 1: **109 of 255 visits arrived after every window closed** (up to 76.8h late), with weekend spillover and even duplicated serves. A control run identical except no `layover_config`: **0 late**. The API spec itself explains it — layover duration "won't influence the cost or duration," i.e., rest time is injected into reported arrival times but **not propagated into window feasibility**. It's built for long-haul trucking without tight windows. The `--layover` flag remains in the script for re-testing if NB fixes this, and the finding is documented in the docstring.

The good news: the layover mechanism turned out to be unnecessary — the per-day windows achieve the daily segmentation you wanted, with feasibility fully enforced.

**Knobs:** `--target-orders` (1000), `--seed`, `--travel-factor` (sizes reps: TRAD×2 + 1 each currently), `--weeks`. One open item: NOTURNO reps currently get the same daytime windows as everyone — the sheet has no hours data. If night sellers should run evening windows, that's a one-line change.

```bash
import json, datetime
TZ = datetime.timezone(datetime.timedelta(hours=-3))
print(f"{'rep':16s} {'jobs':>4s} {'days':>4s} {'late':>4s} {'brks':>4s}  per-day: jobs/hours   [break times]")
for w in (1,2,3,4):

    jobs = {j["id"]: j for j in inp["jobs"]}
    for r in res["routes"]:
        segs, late, brks = {}, 0, []
        for s in r["steps"]:
            if s["type"] == "break":
                bt = datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(s["arrival"], TZ)
                brks.append(bt.strftime("%a %H:%M"))
                continue
            if s["type"] != "job": continue
            tws = jobs[s["id"]]["time_windows"]
            if all(s["arrival"] > tw[1] for tw in tws): late += 1
            start = max(s["arrival"], min((tw[0] for tw in tws if s["arrival"] <= tw[1]), default=s["arrival"]))
            dt = datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(start, TZ)
            d = segs.setdefault(dt.date(), [start, start + s["service"], 0])
            d[0] = min(d[0], start); d[1] = max(d[1], start + s["service"]); d[2] += 1
        n = sum(v[2] for v in segs.values())
        days = "  ".join(f"{dd.strftime('%a')}:{v[2]}/{(v[1]-v[0])/3600:.1f}h" for dd, v in sorted(segs.items()))
        print(f"{r['vehicle']:16s} {n:4d} {len(segs):4d} {late:4d} {len(brks):4d}  {days}")
        if w == 1: print(f"{'':34s}breaks start: {brks}")
    print()
```

### CLAUDE (2026-07-21T15:13:41.879Z)

All four weeks validate cleanly with the breaks model. Final state:

## What ran

Every rep-week vehicle now carries **4 mandatory nightly breaks** (Mon–Thu nights, 10h each, takeable 20:00→07:00) and the audit confirms **all 4 breaks taken on every route** — early break-step arrivals just mean the rep idles until the 20:00 window opens, service starting in-window. The **7.25h × 5 days weekly cap** is encoded structurally as the daily window span (08:00–15:15), which holds exactly: observed day spans max out at 7.4h (7.25h window + trailing service on the last stop).

Across all 4 weeks: **0 unassigned, 0 late arrivals**, type purity intact, TRAD reps working 4–5 days/week (light-workload types 2–4 days), ~2,500–2,700 km/week.

## Why `max_working_time` had to go — tested, not assumed

I ran it exactly as specified first (`max_working_time = 130500`): each rep served **exactly 1 job, 245/250 unassigned**. The route data showed why — break durations land in the `service` bucket (40.1h ≈ 4×10h) and overnight gaps in `waiting` (~42h), and the API counts *service, waiting, setup and driving* all against `max_working_time`. So the mandatory breaks alone (40h) exceed the 36.25h budget before any real work — the two features are arithmetically incompatible on a week-spanning vehicle. This is documented in the script's docstring with the test numbers, alongside the earlier layover finding.

The day-window encoding delivers the same business rule (≤7.25h/day, ≤5 days ⇒ ≤36.25h/week) with hard-constraint guarantees, and rep sizing now uses the 36.25h week.

One side effect worth noting: narrowing days from 7.5h to 7.25h pushed TRAD-01 to use all 5 days including Wednesday (previously near-empty) — the tighter days force better spreading, which is exactly your "as many days as possible" requirement emerging from the constraint structure.

Script is `data/weekly_layover_plan.py` (the name now undersells it — say the word if you want it renamed to `weekly_plan.py`); outputs in `data/weekly_plan_out/` (`assignments.csv`, `territories_summary.csv`, per-week inputs/solutions).

### CLAUDE (2026-07-21T15:26:26.571Z)

Back to per-day rep instances, but now with named reps and pre-defined weekly territories enforced through the optimization. Design decisions grounded in what we've validated so far:

- **Territories**: per week and per tipo, I'll cluster that week's POS into one balanced territory per rep (service-hour-weighted k-means), then lock jobs to their rep via a unique territory skill — the hard-constraint mechanism we've already proven for type purity. Type purity stays implied since territories never cross tipos.
- **Rep-day vehicles**: `'P. GONZALEZ-1-1'` style (week-day suffix), 5 per rep per week, each with the 7.25h day window (08:00–15:15) — no breaks needed since no vehicle spans a night, and the spec confirms `start_index`/`end_index` are optional (open routes).

      })\n\n    body = {\n        \"description\": f\"FEMSA weekly territory plan - week {week}\",\n        \"locations\": {\"id\": 1, \"location\": locations},\n        \"jobs\": jobs,\n        \"vehicles\": vehicles,\n        \"options\": {\"routing\": {\"mode\": \"car\"}},\n    }\n    return body\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------- NB client\n\ndef submit(body, key):\n    url = f\"{NB_SUBMIT}?key={urllib.parse.quote(key)}\"\n    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=json.dumps(body).encode(),\n                                 headers={\"Content-Type\": \"application/json\"})\n    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120) as r:\n        return json.load(r)[\"id\"]\n\n\ndef poll(rid, key):\n    url = f\"{NB_RESULT}?id={urllib.parse.quote(rid)}&key={urllib.parse.quote(key)}\"\n    for _ in range(POLL_MAX):\n        with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=120) as r:\n            data = json.load(r)\n        res = data.get(\"result\") or {}\n        if res.get(\"routes\") is not None or res.get(\"unassigned\") is not None:\n            return res\n        if str(data.get(\"status\", \"\")).lower() in (\"failed\", \"error\"):\n            raise RuntimeError(f\"optimization failed: {json.dumps(data)[:400]}\")\n        time.sleep(POLL_S)\n    raise RuntimeError(\"poll timeout\")\n\n\n# ------------------------------------------------------------ post-process\n\ndef rep_base(vehicle_id):\n    return vehicle_id.rsplit(\"-\", 2)[0]\n\n\ndef summarize(week, result, assign_writer, terr_writer):\n    \"\"\"Aggregate day-vehicle routes back to named reps.\"\"\"\n    day_names = [\"Mon\", \"Tue\", \"Wed\", \"Thu\", \"Fri\"]\n    per_rep = {}\n    for route in result.get(\"routes\", []):\n        veh = route[\"vehicle\"]\n        rep = rep_base(veh)\n        agg = per_rep.setdefault(rep, {d: 0 for d in day_names})\n        for step in route.get(\"steps\", []):\n            if step.get(\"type\") != \"job\":\n                continue\n            arr = datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(step[\"arrival\"], TZ)\n            agg[day_names[arr.weekday()]] += 1\n            assign_writer.writerow([step.get(\"id\"), veh, rep, week,\n                                    arr.date().isoformat(), arr.strftime(\"%H:%M\")])\n    for rep, agg in sorted(per_rep.items()):\n        n = sum(agg.values())\n        if n:\n            terr_writer.writerow([rep, week, n, sum(1 for d in day_names if agg[d])] +\n                                 [agg[d] for d in day_names])\n    return (len(result.get(\"unassigned\", [])), len(per_rep))\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------- main\n\ndef main():\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])\n    ap.add_argument(\"--xlsx\", default=XLSX_DEFAULT)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--target-orders\", type=int, default=1000)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--seed\", type=int, default=42)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--travel-factor\", type=float, default=1.0,\n                    help=\"assumed travel time as a multiple of service time (rep sizing)\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--out-dir\", default=os.path.join(BASE_DIR, \"weekly_plan_out\"))\n    ap.add_argument(\"--weeks\", default=\"1,2,3,4\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--run\", action=\"store_true\", help=\"submit to NB and post-process\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--nb-key\", default=os.environ.get(\"NB_API_KEY\"))\n    args = ap.parse_args()\n\n    rng = random.Random(args.seed)\n    pos, skipped = load_base(args.xlsx)\n    print(f\"base: {len(pos)} usable POS  (skipped: {skipped})\")\n\n    chosen = sample_pos(pos, args.target_orders, rng)\n    total_orders = sum(orders_per_cycle(p[\"freq\"]) for p in chosen)\n    mix = {}\n    for p in chosen:\n        mix[p[\"tipo\"]] = mix.get(p[\"tipo\"], 0) + orders_per_cycle(p[\"freq\"])\n    print(f\"sampled: {len(chosen)} POS -> {total_orders} orders over 4 weeks\")\n    for t, n in sorted(mix.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1]):\n        print(f\"    {n:5d} orders  {t}\")\n\n    visits = expand_visits(chosen, rng)\n    rep_names_by_tipo, terr = design_territories(visits, args.travel_factor, rng)\n    print(\"rep roster:\")\n    for tipo, names in sorted(rep_names_by_tipo.items()):\n        print(f\"    {tipo}: {', '.join(names)}\")\n\n    os.makedirs(args.out_dir, exist_ok=True)\n    weeks = [int(w) for w in args.weeks.split(\",\")]\n\n    # territory definition file: one row per POS per week\n    with open(os.path.join(args.out_dir, \"territories.csv\"), \"w\", newline=\"\") as f:\n        tw = csv.writer(f)\n        tw.writerow([\"week\", \"rep\", \"tipo\", \"matricula\", \"lat\", \"lng\", \"service_s\"])\n        pos_by_m = {p[\"matricula\"]: p for p in chosen}\n        for (w, tipo), t in sorted(terr.items()):\n            for m, rep_idx in sorted(t[\"assign\"].items()):\n                p = pos_by_m[m]\n                tw.writerow([w, rep_names_by_tipo[tipo][rep_idx], tipo, m,\n                             p[\"lat\"], p[\"lng\"], p[\"service\"]])\n\n    inputs = {}\n    for w in weeks:\n        body = build_week_input(w, visits[w], rep_names_by_tipo, terr)\n        path = os.path.join(args.out_dir, f\"week_{w}_input.json\")\n        with open(path, \"w\") as f:\n            json.dump(body, f, indent=1)\n        inputs[w] = body\n        print(f\"week {w}: {len(body['jobs'])} jobs, {len(body['vehicles'])} rep-day vehicles -> {os.path.basename(path)}\")\n\n    if not args.run:\n        print(\"\\n(inputs only; re-run with --run to optimize)\")\n        return\n\n    if not args.nb_key:\n        sys.exit(\"--run requires $NB_API_KEY or --nb-key\")\n\n    assign_f = open(os.path.join(args.out_dir, \"assignments.csv\"), \"w\", newline=\"\")\n    terr_f = open(os.path.join(args.out_dir, \"territories_summary.csv\"), \"w\", newline=\"\")\n    aw, tw = csv.writer(assign_f), csv.writer(terr_f)\n    aw.writerow([\"job_id\", \"vehicle\", \"rep\", \"week\", \"date\", \"arrival\"])\n    tw.writerow([\"rep\", \"week\", \"jobs\", \"days_worked\", \"Mon\", \"Tue\", \"Wed\", \"Thu\", \"Fri\"])\n\n    for w in weeks:\n        rid = submit(inputs[w], args.nb_key)\n        print(f\"week {w}: submitted {rid}, polling...\")\n        result = poll(rid, args.nb_key)\n        with open(os.path.join(args.out_dir, f\"week_{w}_solution.json\"), \"w\") as f:\n            json.dump(result, f)\n        unassigned, reps_used = summarize(w, result, aw, tw)\n        summ = result.get(\"summary\", {})\n        print(f\"week {w}: {reps_used} reps active, {unassigned} unassigned, \"\n              f\"distance {summ.get('distance', 0) / 1000:.0f} km\")\n\n    assign_f.close()\n    terr_f.close()\n    print(f\"\\nwrote {args.out_dir}/territories.csv, assignments.csv, territories_summary.csv\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n"
```json
}
```

### CLAUDE (2026-07-21T15:29:44.608Z)

Complete and fully validated. **1,021 visits served across 4 weeks: 0 unassigned, 0 late arrivals, 0 territory violations** — every job was served by exactly the named rep whose territory it belongs to.

## The v3 model

- **Rep-day vehicles, named as specified:** `P. GONZALEZ-1-1` = week 1 Monday … `-1-5` = Friday. 25 vehicles per week (5 reps × 5 days), each a 7.25h shift (08:00–15:15), **no start/end index** — open routes beginning at the first client. Breaks and layovers are gone; nothing spans a night anymore.
- **Stable roster across weeks:** P. GONZALEZ + M. SILVA (TRADICIONAL), A. SANTOS (NOTURNO), C. SOUZA (OFF FRAGMENTADO), J. OLIVEIRA (AUTOSSERVICO). Name blocks are tipo-bound, so a name never changes seller type.
- **Territories drive the optimization:** per week and tipo, that week's POS are clustered into service-hour-balanced territories (pure-python weighted k-means, 20% headroom), and each job carries its territory id as a skill that only its rep's 5 day-vehicles hold. Type purity is implied since territories never span tipos.

## Results

- **Every rep works all 5 days in every week** — the per-day instances plus open routes made full-week spreading natural (the previous week-vehicle model left light reps bunched into 2–3 days).
- Weekly distance dropped to **833–972 km** from ~2,500–2,700 in the week-vehicle model — no depot legs, and reps stay inside compact territories.
- Workloads: TRAD reps ~78–123 visits/week, lighter types 13–26 — proportional to their order volumes.

**Outputs** in `weekly_plan_out/`: `territories.csv` (week, rep, POS, coords — the territory definitions), `assignments.csv` (visit → rep-day vehicle, date, arrival), `territories_summary.csv` (per rep-week day counts, shown above), plus per-week inputs/solutions.

One design note: territories are re-clustered each week because the POS mix changes (0.5/0.25-frequency clients come and go), so e.g. the TRAD split shifts between P. GONZALEZ and M. SILVA week to week (117/79 in W1, 80/123 in W2). If you'd rather have **fixed territories across the whole 4-week cycle** (same geography every week, only the visit list changing), that's a small change — cluster once on the full sampled POS set instead of per week. Want that?

Pure python; fine for POC sizes.\"\"\"\n    if k == 1:\n        return [0] * len(points)\n    cap = sum(p[\"weight\"] for p in points) / k * CLUSTER_HEADROOM\n    # k-means++ style seeding\n    cents = [rng.choice(points)]\n    while len(cents) < k:\n        dists = [min((p[\"lat\"] - c[\"lat\"]) ** 2 + (p[\"lng\"] - c[\"lng\"]) ** 2 for c in cents) for p in points]\n        tot = sum(dists) or 1.0\n        r, acc, pick = rng.random() * tot, 0.0, points[-1]\n        for p, d in zip(points, dists):\n            acc += d\n            if acc >= r:\n                pick = p\n                break\n        cents.append(pick)\n    cents = [(c[\"lat\"], c[\"lng\"]) for c in cents]\n\n    assign = [0] * len(points)\n    for _ in range(iters):\n        # order points by how much they prefer their best centroid (regret)\n        order = sorted(range(len(points)), key=lambda i: -_regret(points[i], cents))\n        load = [0.0] * k\n        newassign = [0] * len(points)\n        for i in order:\n            p = points[i]\n            ranked = sorted(range(k), key=lambda c: (p[\"lat\"] - cents[c][0]) ** 2 + (p[\"lng\"] - cents[c][1]) ** 2)\n            target = next((c for c in ranked if load[c] + p[\"weight\"] <= cap), ranked[0])\n            newassign[i] = target\n            load[target] += p[\"weight\"]\n        if newassign == assign:\n            break\n        assign = newassign\n        for c in range(k):\n            members = [points[i] for i in range(len(points)) if assign[i] == c]\n            if members:\n                cents[c] = (sum(m[\"lat\"] for m in members) / len(members),\n                            sum(m[\"lng\"] for m in members) / len(members))\n    return assign\n\n\ndef _regret(p, cents):\n    d = sorted((p[\"lat\"] - c[0]) ** 2 + (p[\"lng\"] - c[1]) ** 2 for c in cents)\n    return (d[1] - d[0]) if len(d) > 1 else d[0]",

Returns (assign, cells) where\n    assign[i] = cell index (argmin ||p-c||^2 - w), and cells = list of convex\n    polygons [(x,y)..] that are pairwise disjoint by construction and cover\n    the bounding box of the points.\n    \"\"\"\n    if k == 1:\n        xs, ys = [p[\"x\"] for p in points], [p[\"y\"] for p in points]\n        m = 0.05\n        box = [(min(xs) - m, min(ys) - m), (max(xs) - m * -1 + 0, min(ys) - m),\n               (max(xs) + m, max(ys) + m), (min(xs) - m, max(ys) + m)]\n        box = [(min(xs) - m, min(ys) - m), (max(xs) + m, min(ys) - m),\n               (max(xs) + m, max(ys) + m), (min(xs) - m, max(ys) + m)]\n        return [0] * len(points), [box]\n\n    total_w = sum(p[\"weight\"] for p in points)\n    target = total_w / k\n\n    # k-means++ seeding + a few Lloyd steps for sane centroids\n    cents = [(rng.choice(points)[\"x\"], rng.choice(points)[\"y\"])]\n    cents = [(points[rng.randrange(len(points))][\"x\"], points[rng.randrange(len(points))][\"y\"])]\n    while len(cents) < k:\n        d2 = [min((p[\"x\"] - cx) ** 2 + (p[\"y\"] - cy) ** 2 for cx, cy in cents) for p in points]\n        tot = sum(d2) or 1.0\n        r, acc, pick = rng.random() * tot, 0.0, len(points) - 1\n        for i, d in enumerate(d2):\n            acc += d\n            if acc >= r:\n                pick = i\n                break\n        cents.append((points[pick][\"x\"], points[pick][\"y\"]))\n    for _ in range(8):\n        groups = [[] for _ in range(k)]\n        for p in points:\n            ci = min(range(k), key=lambda c: (p[\"x\"] - loads[c]) / target\n        eta *= 0.97\n\n    # cell polygons: bbox clipped by pairwise power bisector half-planes\n    xs, ys = [p[\"x\"] for p in points], [p[\"y\"] for p in points]\n    m = 0.05\n    bbox = [(min(xs) - m, min(ys) - m), (max(xs) + m, min(ys) - m),\n            (max(xs) + m, max(ys) + m), (min(xs) - m, max(ys) + m)]\n    cells = []\n    for i in range(k):\n        poly = list(bbox)\n        cxi, cyi = cents[i]\n        for j in range(k):\n            if i == j or not poly:\n                continue\n            cxj, cyj = cents[j]\n            # ||p-ci||^2 - wi <= ||p-cj||^2 - wj  =>  2(cj-ci).p <= |cj|^2-|ci|^2 - (wj-wi)... rearranged:\n            a, b = 2 * (cxj - cxi), 2 * (cyj - cyi)\n            c = (cxj ** 2 + cyj ** 2) - (cxi ** 2 + cyi ** 2) - (w[j] - import json, csv, itertools
```bash
def pip(pt, ring):  # point-in-polygon (ray cast), ring = [[lng,lat]..]
    x, y = pt; inside = False
    for i in range(len(ring) - 1):
        x1, y1 = ring[i]; x2, y2 = ring[i + 1]
        if (y1 > y) != (y2 > y) and x < (x2 - x1) * (y - y1) / (y2 - y1) + x1:
            inside = not inside
    return inside

gj = json.load(open("weekly_plan_out/territories.geojson"))
feats = gj["features"]
terr_pos = {}  # (week, rep) -> [(lng,lat)]
rep_zone = {}
for row in csv.DictReader(open("weekly_plan_out/territories.csv")):
    terr_pos.setdefault((int(row["week"]), row["rep"]), []).append((float(row["lng"]), float(row["lat"])))

bad_contain = 0; checked = 0
for f in feats:
    ring = f["geometry"]["coordinates"][0]
    for pt in terr_pos.get((f["properties"]["week"], f["properties"]["rep"]), []):
        checked += 1
        if not pip(pt, ring): bad_contain += 1

# disjointness within (week,tipo): each rep's POS must NOT fall in a sibling's polygon
bad_overlap = 0
by_wt = {}
for f in feats:
    by_wt.setdefault((f["properties"]["week"], f["properties"]["tipo"]), []).append(f)
for (w, tipo), fs in by_wt.items():
    for f in fs:
        ring = f["geometry"]["coordinates"][0]
        for g in fs:
            if g is f: continue
            for pt in terr_pos.get((w, g["properties"]["rep"]), []):
                if pip(pt, ring): bad_overlap += 1

# balance: service hours per territory
loads = {}
for row in csv.DictReader(open("weekly_plan_out/territories.csv")):
    k = (int(row["week"]), row["rep"])
    loads[k] = loads.get(k, 0) + int(row["service_s"]) / 3600
print(f"POS-in-own-polygon: {checked - bad_contain}/{checked} | POS inside a sibling territory: {bad_overlap}")
print("service-hours per rep-territory by week:")
for w in (1, 2, 3, 4):
    row = "  ".join(f"{rep.split()[1]}:{h:.1f}h" for (wk, rep), h in sorted(loads.items()) if wk == w)
    print(f"  W{w}: {row}")
```

### CLAUDE (2026-07-21T15:41:09.798Z)

Done and fully validated with zones active. **1,021 visits served, 0 unassigned, 0 late, 0 territory violations** across all 4 weeks.

## What changed

**Non-overlapping territories, by construction.** The clustering is now a service-hour-balanced **power diagram**: each rep's territory is a convex polygon cell, assignment = cell membership, and same-tipo cells are geometrically disjoint half-plane partitions — overlap is impossible rather than merely penalized. The offline audit confirms it: 885/885 POS-week placements inside their own polygon, 0 inside a sibling's. Workload balance held (TRAD split: SILVA 12.4–14.8h vs GONZALEZ 11.0–14.3h of service across weeks). One caveat to be explicit about: disjointness is **within each seller type** — across tipos, territories are separate layers over the same city (a NOTURNO territory unavoidably covers the same ground as TRADICIONAL ones, since both client types span the whole region).

**Zones in the input JSON.** Each weekly input now carries a `zones` array — one GeoJSON Polygon per rep-territory with the rep's name in the description (`"P. GONZALEZ (VEND. TRADICIONAL) week 1"`), renderable directly on a map. The zones are also *enforced*: jobs carry `zones: [id]`, vehicles carry `allowed_zones: [id]`, and the same id doubles as a skill — two independent locks. The API accepted all of it and the solutions honor the territories exactly.

**Also written:** `weekly_plan_out/territories.geojson` — a FeatureCollection of all 20 territory polygons (properties: week, rep, tipo, zone_id) you can drop straight into any map viewer (geojson.io, Leaflet, QGIS).

Cost of the geometric guarantee: weekly distance ticked up slightly (912–1,022 km vs 833–972 with free clustering) — convex disjoint cells are marginally less travel-optimal than unconstrained assignment. Structure held otherwise: every rep works all 5 days, every week.

### CLAUDE (2026-07-21T17:51:39.957Z)

Here's the full breakdown, verified by replicating the builder's logic against the source workbook — the computed value matches the input exactly.

## How vehicle 12155 gets `skills: [3, 4, 5, 7]`

**Step 1 — What the vehicle is.** Equipment row 12155 in the workbook has Equipment Type `MSU-35 - MSU-35 CDL`; the builder (`scripts/build-rp-input.mjs`) extracts the leading type code → **`MSU-35`**.

**Step 2 — Skill numbering.** Each Order Class ID from the "Order Classes" sheet maps to a skill integer: the 19 class IDs are sorted alphabetically and numbered 1–19 (`9`→1, `A`→2, `C`→3, `D`→4, `DEL`→5, `E`→6, `F`→7, `G`→8, … `Z`→19). The numbers themselves are arbitrary but stable/reproducible.

**Step 3 — Eligibility per class.** Each class's "Equipment Type Restrictions" cell is parsed as either `Allowed: <list>` (only listed types may serve it; a bare "Allowed: All" parses to an empty list = no restriction) or `Disallowed: <list>` (everyone except listed types). The vehicle gets the skill of every class its type is eligible for:

| Skill | Class | Description | Restriction | MSU-35 eligible? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | C | ONSITE | Allowed: **MSU-35**, MSU, MSU-25… | ✅ explicitly allowed |
| 4 | D | OFFSITE | Allowed: All | ✅ unrestricted |
| 5 | DEL | DELIVERY | Allowed: All | ✅ unrestricted |
| 7 | F | PLASTICS / MEDIA | Allowed: All | ✅ unrestricted |
| 1,2,6,8–13,17–19 | 9,A,E,G,H,N,P,R,S,W,Y,Z | (deliveries, pickups, supplies…) | **Disallowed: MSU-35**, TIP1, TIP3… | ❌ explicitly disallowed |
| 14,15 | T,U | DATA TAPE / HARD DRIVE SHRED SITAD | Allowed: MSU, MDS3-33HD… (not MSU-35) | ❌ not in allow list |
| 16 | V | PICKUP SITAD | Allowed: ALM types (+RM20 override) | ❌ not in allow list |

So the MSU-35 shred truck can do **Onsite shredding (C)** — where it's explicitly named — plus the three unrestricted classes **Offsite (D), Delivery (DEL), Plastics/Media (F)**, and is barred from all the box-truck-style work (pickups, supply drops, rush/next-day deliveries) where `MSU-35` appears on the Disallowed list.

**Step 4 — How it binds.** Each job requires exactly one skill: its own Order Class's number (`skills: [<class skill>]`; class-less orders get no requirement). NB then only assigns a job to a vehicle whose skill set contains it — so 12155 can only receive C/D/DEL/F orders.

One nuance worth knowing: for classes T and U, the *description text* mentions "MSU-35 CDL HARD DRIVE SHREDDER", but the type *code* there is `MDS3-33HD` — the parser correctly keys on codes, so vehicle 12155 (code `MSU-35`) is not eligible. And the `FORCE_ALLOWED = { V: ["RM20"] }` override in the builder (customer-requested) only touches class V/RM20, so it doesn't affect this vehicle.

### CLAUDE (2026-07-21T18:35:06.586Z)

Both files are created and verified: `data/jobs_new.csv` (397 jobs) and `data/vehicles_new.csv` (50 vehicles).

Along the way I found and fixed a real gap: the new input JSON had **no breaks on any vehicle**. It turns out `build-rp-input.mjs` never emitted breaks — the old input's breaks (11:00–14:00, 1h, on all 24 vehicles) had been added by some earlier step outside the script — and `json-to-csvs.mjs` papered over it with a hardcoded `2026-05-29T11:00` break, which would have written wrong dates into your new CSVs. Fixes, all rule-preserving:

- **`build-rp-input.mjs`** now emits the break on every vehicle, anchored to `--date` — window 11:00–14:00 local, 3600s, matching the original input JSON's values exactly (overridable via `--break-window` / `--break-service`). `input_iron_mountain_new.json` was rebuilt and all 50 vehicles now carry it on 2026-07-10.
- **`json-to-csvs.mjs`** now reads break columns from each vehicle's `breaks[0]` in the input JSON instead of the hardcoded constant, and gained `--suffix` (for the `_new` filenames) plus `--locations-workbook`/`--locations-sheet` so the job `description` column resolves Location Name IDs from the day-2 workbook's tab.

Spot-checks pass: vehicle 12155 shows shift `2026-07-10T04:00–22:00`, break `2026-07-10T11:00–14:00` (3600s), skills `3,4,5,7`; jobs carry the resolved location descriptions (e.g. `176778|W`), 7/10 time windows (up to 2 pairs), and class-consistent skills. The CSV headers match the existing `jobs.csv`/`vehicles.csv` format, so anything downstream of those will accept these files unchanged.

### CLAUDE (2026-07-21T18:37:12.340Z)

All 12 errors are fixed, and both CSVs were regenerated from the corrected input.

**Root cause:** the source workbook itself — 12 order rows in "7102026 Orders" have SW2 Open/Close **transposed** (e.g. `CDD6-305372583`: SW2 Open `21:00`, Close `14:00`). Each sits alongside a morning SW1 window (`09:00–13:30`), so the intent is clearly an afternoon window written backwards. An inverted window (end ≤ start) is invalid for the optimizer.

**Fix:** `parseWindowSec` in `build-rp-input.mjs` now treats an inverted open/close pair as swapped (`close < open` → `[close, open]`) and reports how many it repaired — the build log now shows `repaired inverted open/close windows: 12`. The existing special rules (close = 00:00 → end-of-day, etc.) are untouched.

**Verified after rebuild:** 0 inverted windows remain; the named jobs now read sensibly —
- `CDD6-305372583`: `09:00–13:30` + `14:00–21:00`
- `CDD6-305372446`: `00:00–13:30` + `14:00–23:59`
- `CDD6-305373391`: `07:00–12:00` + `13:00–16:00`

`jobs_new.csv` / `vehicles_new.csv` were regenerated from the repaired JSON, so their `tw_start_2`/`tw_end_2` columns carry the corrected windows too. Everything else in the build is byte-for-byte the same rules (397 jobs, 50 vehicles, same skills).

Worth flagging upstream to Iron Mountain: the transposition is in their export (the sheet's own header even orders the columns `SW2 Close Time` before `SW2 Open Time`), so future day-files may carry the same defect — the builder now self-heals it either way.

### CLAUDE (2026-07-21T18:45:04.200Z)

`data/depots_new.csv` is created — 29 rows, one per `depots[]` entry in the input JSON.

I added a depots emission to `json-to-csvs.mjs` (same pattern as jobs/vehicles, honoring the `--suffix` flag), so all three CSVs now come from one run. Columns: `id, description, latitude, longitude, address_line_1, city, state, zip` — coordinates resolved from `input.locations` via each depot's `location_index`, address fields joined from the master workbook's Depots tab. `jobs_new.csv` and `vehicles_new.csv` were regenerated in the same run, unchanged.

One data note visible in the sample: some depot rows have gaps in the master data itself (e.g. `CD-D3` has no postal code) — those cells are left blank rather than invented.

The static depot-allocation\n// maps (public/depot_allocation_map_6*.html) reference tiles via\n// /api/map-proxy/maps/... instead of api.nextbillion.io/...?key=<key>.\nexport async function GET(\n  req: Request,\n  { params }: { params: Promise<{ path: string[] }> }\n) {\n  const apiKey = process.env.NB_API_KEY;\n  if (!apiKey) return new Response(\"NB_API_KEY not configured\", { status: 500 });\n\n  const { path } = await params;\n  const url = new URL(req.url);\n  const target = new URL(`https://api.nextbillion.io/${path.join(\"/\")}`);\n  url.searchParams.forEach((v, k) => {\n    if (k !== \"key\") target.searchParams.set(k, v);\n  });\n  target.searchParams.set(\"key\", apiKey);\n\n  const r = await fetch(target, {\n    headers: { accept: req.headers.get(\"accept\") ?? \"*/*\" },\n  });\n  return new Response(r.body, {\n    status: r.status,\n    headers: {\n      \"content-type\": r.headers.get(\"content-type\") ?? \"application/octet-stream\",\n      \"cache-control\": \"public, max-age=86400\",\n    },\n  });\n}\n"

```json
 "content": "export function fmtTime(unixSec?: number): string {\n  if (unixSec == null || !Number.isFinite(unixSec)) return \"—\";\n  const d = new Date(unixSec * 1000);\n  return d.toLocaleString(\"en-US\", {\n    timeZone: \"America/Detroit\",\n    month: \"2-digit\",\n    day: \"2-digit\",\n    hour: \"2-digit\",\n    minute: \"2-digit\",\n    hour12: false,\n  });\n}\n\nexport function fmtTimeOnly(unixSec?: number): string {\n  if (unixSec == null || !Number.isFinite(unixSec)) return \"—\";\n  const d = new Date(unixSec * 1000);\n  return d.toLocaleString(\"en-US\", {\n    timeZone: \"America/Detroit\",\n    hour: \"2-digit\",\n    minute: \"2-digit\",\n    hour12: false,\n  });\n}\n\nexport function fmtMin(sec?: number): string {\n  if (sec == null) return \"—\";\n  return `${Math.round(sec / 60)} min`;\n}\n\nexport function fmtKm(m?: number): string {\n  if (m == null) return \"—\";\n  return `${(m / 1000).toFixed(1)} km`;\n}\n"
}
```

```json
 "content": "\"use client\";\n\nimport { useMemo, useRef, useState } from \"react\";\nimport { fmtKm, fmtMin } from \"@/lib/format\";\n\nexport interface RouteFileSummary {\n  fileName: string;\n  regionId: string;\n  regionName: string;\n  routeId: string | number;\n  routeDate: string;\n  plannedDeparture: string;\n  stopCount: number;\n}\n\ninterface BatchSide {\n  distance?: number;\n  duration?: number;\n  service?: number;\n  unassigned: number;\n  noRoutes: boolean;\n  error?: string;\n}\n\ninterface BatchRow {\n  fileName: string;\n  regionId: string;\n  routeId: string | number;\n  routeDate: string;\n  stopCount: number;\n  status: \"queued\" | \"running\" | \"done\" | \"error\";\n  error?: string;\n  fixed?: BatchSide;\n  free?: BatchSide;\n}\n\nconst CONCURRENCY = 3;\nconst POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 3000;\nconst MAX_POLL_ATTEMPTS = 100; // ~5 minutes per optimization job\n\nasync function pollResult(\n  id: string,\n  canceller: { cancelled: boolean }\n): Promise<Record<string, unknown>> {\n  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < MAX_POLL_ATTEMPTS; attempt++) {\n    if (canceller.cancelled) throw new Error(\"cancelled\");\n    const r = await fetch(`/api/optimize/result?id=${encodeURIComponent(id)}`);\n    const data = await r.json();\n    if (data.status === \"done\") return data.result;\n    if (data.status === \"error\") throw new Error(data.error || \"optimization failed\");\n    await new Promise((res) => setTimeout(res, POLL_INTERVAL_MS));\n  }\n  throw new Error(\"timed out waiting for result\");\n}\n\nfunction sideFromResult(result: Record<string, unknown>): BatchSide {\n  const summary = (result?.summary ?? {}) as {\n    distance?: number;\n    duration?: number;\n    service?: number;\n  };\n  const routes = Array.isArray(result?.routes) ? (result.routes as unknown[]) : [];\n  const unassigned = Array.isArray(result?.unassigned)\n    ? (result.unassigned as unknown[]).length\n    : 0;\n  return {\n    distance: summary.distance,\n    duration: summary.duration,\n    service: summary.service,\n    unassigned,\n    noRoutes: routes.length === 0,\n  };\n}\n\nfunction sideOk(s?: BatchSide): s is BatchSide & { distance: number; duration: number } {\n  return s != null && !s.error && !s.noRoutes && s.distance != null && s.duration != null;\n}\n\nfunction pctSavings(fixed: number, free: number): number | null {\n  if (!Number.isFinite(fixed) || fixed <= 0) return null;\n  return ((fixed - free) / fixed) * 100;\n}\n\nfunction fmtPct(p: number | null): string {\n  if (p == null) return \"—\";\n  return `${p >= 0 ? \"\" : \"+\"}${Math.abs(p).toFixed(1)}%${p >= 0 ? \" saved\" : \" worse\"}`;\n}\n\nexport default function FullRun({ files }: { files: RouteFileSummary[] }) {\n  const [filterRegion, setFilterRegion] = useState<string>(\"all\");\n  const [rows, setRows] = useState<BatchRow[]>([]);\n  const [running, setRunning] = useState(false);\n  const cancelRef = useRef<{ cancelled: boolean }>({ cancelled: false });\n\n  const regions = useMemo(() => {\n    const set = new Set(files.map((f) => f.regionId));\n    return Array.from(set).sort();\n  }, [files]);\n\n  const filteredFiles = useMemo(() => {\n    if (filterRegion === \"all\") return files;\n    return files.filter((f) => f.regionId === filterRegion);\n  }, [files, filterRegion]);\n\n  const finished = rows.filter((r) => r.status === \"done\" || r.status === \"error\").length;\n\n  function updateRow(fileName: string, patch: Partial<BatchRow>) {\n    setRows((prev) => prev.map((r) => (r.fileName === fileName ? { ...r, ...patch } : r)));\n  }\n\n  async function processFile(file: RouteFileSummary, canceller: { cancelled: boolean }) {\n    updateRow(file.fileName, { status: \"running\" });\n    try {\n      const submit = await fetch(\"/api/optimize\", {\n        method: \"POST\",\n        headers: { \"Content-Type\": \"application/json\" },\n        body: JSON.stringify({ fileName: file.fileName }),\n      });\n      const text = await submit.text();\n      if (!submit.ok) throw new Error(`submit ${submit.status}: ${text.slice(0, 200)}`);\n      const data = JSON.parse(text) as {\n        fixed: { id?: string; error?: string };\n        free: { id?: string; error?: string };\n      };\n\n      const [fixed, free] = await Promise.all(\n        [data.fixed, data.free].map(async (side): Promise<BatchSide> => {\n          if (!side.id) {\n            return { unassigned: 0, noRoutes: true, error: side.error || \"submit failed\" };\n          }\n          try {\n            return sideFromResult(await pollResult(side.id, canceller));\n          } catch (e) {\n            return {\n              unassigned: 0,\n              noRoutes: true,\n              error: e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e),\n            };\n          }\n        })\n      );\n\n      if (canceller.cancelled) return;\n      const sideError = fixed.error ?? free.error;\n      updateRow(file.fileName, {\n        status: sideError && fixed.error && free.error ? \"error\" : \"done\",\n        error: sideError,\n        fixed,\n        free,\n      });\n    } catch (e) {\n      if (canceller.cancelled) return;\n      updateRow(file.fileName, {\n        status: \"error\",\n        error: e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e),\n      });\n    }\n  }\n\n  async function runAll() {\n    cancelRef.current.cancelled = true;\n    const canceller = { cancelled: false };\n    cancelRef.current = canceller;\n\n    const targets = filteredFiles;\n    setRows(\n      targets.map((f) => ({\n        fileName: f.fileName,\n        regionId: f.regionId,\n        routeId: f.routeId,\n        routeDate: f.routeDate,\n        stopCount: f.stopCount,\n        status: \"queued\",\n      }))\n    );\n    setRunning(true);\n\n    let next = 0;\n    const workers = Array.from({ length: Math.min(CONCURRENCY, targets.length) }, async () => {\n      while (!canceller.cancelled) {\n        const idx = next++;\n        if (idx >= targets.length) return;\n        await processFile(targets[idx], canceller);\n      }\n    });\n    await Promise.all(workers);\n    if (!canceller.cancelled) setRunning(false);\n  }\n\n  function cancel() {\n    cancelRef.current.cancelled = true;\n    setRunning(false);\n    setRows((prev) =>\n      prev.map((r) =>\n        r.status === \"queued\" || r.status === \"running\"\n          ? { ...r, status: \"error\", error: \"cancelled\" }\n          : r\n      )\n    );\n  }\n\n  function exportCsv() {\n    const header = [\n      \"region\",\n      \"route_id\",\n      \"route_date\",\n      \"stops\",\n      \"status\",\n      \"fixed_distance_m\",\n      \"free_distance_m\",\n      \"distance_savings_pct\",\n      \"fixed_duration_sec\",\n      \"free_duration_sec\",\n      \"duration_savings_pct\",\n      \"fixed_unassigned\",\n      \"free_unassigned\",\n      \"error\",\n      \"file_name\",\n    ];\n    const lines = [header.join(\",\")];\n    for (const r of rows) {\n      const comparable = sideOk(r.fixed) && sideOk(r.free);\n      const dPct = comparable ? pctSavings(r.fixed!.distance!, r.free!.distance!) : null;\n      const tPct = comparable ? pctSavings(r.fixed!.duration!, r.free!.duration!) : null;\n      lines.push(\n        [\n          r.regionId,\n          String(r.routeId),\n          r.routeDate,\n          r.stopCount,\n          r.status,\n          r.fixed?.distance ?? \"\",\n          r.free?.distance ?? \"\",\n          dPct != null ? dPct.toFixed(2) : \"\",\n          r.fixed?.duration ?? \"\",\n          r.free?.duration ?? \"\",\n          tPct != null ? tPct.toFixed(2) : \"\",\n          r.fixed?.unassigned ?? \"\",\n          r.free?.unassigned ?? \"\",\n          r.error ? `\"${r.error.replace(/\"/g, '\"\"')}\"` : \"\",\n          r.fileName,\n        ].join(\",\")\n      );\n    }\n    const blob = new Blob([lines.join(\"\\n\")], { type: \"text/csv\" });\n    const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);\n    const a = document.createElement(\"a\");\n    a.href = url;\n    a.download = `glwas_full_run_${filterRegion}_${rows.length}_routes.csv`;\n    a.click();\n    URL.revokeObjectURL(url);\n  }\n\n  const totals = useMemo(() => {\n    const comparable = rows.filter((r) => sideOk(r.fixed) && sideOk(r.free));\n    if (comparable.length === 0) return null;\n    const sum = (pick: (r: BatchRow) => number) =>\n      comparable.reduce((acc, r) => acc + pick(r), 0);\n    const fixedDist = sum((r) => r.fixed!.distance!);\n    const freeDist = sum((r) => r.free!.distance!);\n    const fixedDur = sum((r) => r.fixed!.duration!);\n    const freeDur = sum((r) => r.free!.duration!);\n    return {\n      count: comparable.length,\n      fixedDist,\n      freeDist,\n      fixedDur,\n      freeDur,\n      distPct: pctSavings(fixedDist, freeDist),\n      durPct: pctSavings(fixedDur, freeDur),\n    };\n  }, [rows]);\n\n  return (\n    <div className=\"space-y-4\">\n      <section className=\"bg-white border rounded-lg p-4 space-y-3\">\n        <div className=\"flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3\">\n          <label className=\"text-sm font-medium\">Region:</label>\n          <select\n            className=\"border rounded px-2 py-1 text-sm\"\n            value={filterRegion}\n            disabled={running}\n            onChange={(e) => setFilterRegion(e.target.value)}\n          >\n            <option value=\"all\">All ({files.length})</option>\n            {regions.map((r) => (\n              <option key={r} value={r}>\n                {r} ({files.filter((f) => f.regionId === r).length})\n              </option>\n            ))}\n          </select>\n          <button\n            onClick={runAll}\n            disabled={running || filteredFiles.length === 0}\n            className=\"bg-blue-600 hover:bg-blue-700 disabled:bg-gray-400 text-white text-sm font-medium px-4 py-1.5 rounded\"\n          >\n            {running\n              ? `Running… (${finished}/${rows.length})`\n              : `Run all (${filteredFiles.length} routes)`}\n          </button>\n          {running && (\n            <button\n              onClick={cancel}\n              className=\"border border-red-300 text-red-700 hover:bg-red-50 text-sm font-medium px-4 py-1.5 rounded\"\n            >\n              Cancel\n            </button>\n          )}\n          {rows.length > 0 && !running && (\n            <button\n              onClick={exportCsv}\n              className=\"border border-gray-300 text-gray-700 hover:bg-gray-50 text-sm font-medium px-4 py-1.5 rounded\"\n            >\n              Export CSV\n            </button>\n          )}\n        </div>\n        <p className=\"text-xs text-gray-500\">\n          Runs the fixed-vs-free comparison for every route in the selection ({CONCURRENCY} routes\n          in flight at a time; each route submits two optimization jobs). Savings compare the\n          planned (fixed) sequence against the NB-optimized (free) sequence.\n        </p>\n        {rows.length > 0 && (\n          <div className=\"h-2 bg-gray-100 rounded overflow-hidden\">\n            <div\n              className=\"h-full bg-blue-500 transition-all\"\n              style={{ width: `${rows.length ? pctSavings(r.fixed!.distance!, r.free!.distance!)\n                  : null;\n                const tPct = comparable\n                  ? pctSavings(r.fixed!.duration!, r.free!.duration!)\n                  : null;\n                const unassignedMismatch =\n                  (r.fixed?.unassigned ?? 0) !== (r.free?.unassigned ?? 0);\n                return (\n                  <tr\n                    key={r.fileName}\n                    className={`border-b last:border-b-0 ${\n                      unassignedMismatch && r.status === \"done\" ? \"bg-amber-50\" : \"\"\n                    }`}\n                  >\n                    <td className=\"p-2\">{r.regionId}</td>\n                    <td className=\"p-2\">{String(r.routeId)}</td>\n                    <td className=\"p-2 font-mono text-xs\">{r.routeDate}</td>\n                    <td className=\"p-2 text-right\">{r.stopCount}</td>\n                    <td className=\"p-2 text-right font-mono\">{fmtKm(r.fixed?.distance)}</td>\n                    <td className=\"p-2 text-right font-mono\">{fmtKm(r.free?.distance)}</td>\n                    <td\n                      className={`p-2 text-right font-mono ${\n                        dPct == null ? \"\" : dPct >= 0 ? \"text-green-700\" : \"text-red-700\"\n                      }`}\n                    >\n                      {fmtPct(dPct)}\n                    </td>\n                    <td className=\"p-2 text-right font-mono\">{fmtMin(r.fixed?.duration)}</td>\n                    <td className=\"p-2 text-right font-mono\">{fmtMin(r.free?.duration)}</td>\n                    <td\n                      className={`p-2 text-right font-mono ${\n                        tPct == null ? \"\" : tPct >= 0 ? \"text-green-700\" : \"text-red-700\"\n                      }`}\n                    >\n                      {fmtPct(tPct)}\n                    </td>\n                    <td className=\"p-2 text-right font-mono\">\n                      {r.fixed || r.free\n                        ? `${r.fixed?.unassigned ?? \"—\"} / ${r.free?.unassigned ?? \"—\"}`\n                        : \"—\"}\n                    </td>\n                    <td className=\"p-2\">\n                      <RowStatus row={r} />\n                    </td>\n                  </tr>\n                );\n              })}\n            </tbody>\n            {totals && (\n              <tfoot>\n                <tr className=\"border-t-2 font-medium bg-gray-50\">\n                  <td className=\"p-2\" colSpan={4}>\n                    Totals ({totals.count} comparable routes)\n                  </td>\n                  <td className=\"p-2 text-right font-mono\">{fmtKm(totals.fixedDist)}</td>\n                  <td className=\"p-2 text-right font-mono\">{fmtKm(totals.freeDist)}</td>\n                  <td\n                    className={`p-2 text-right font-mono ${\n                      totals.distPct == null\n                        ? \"\"\n                        : totals.distPct >= 0\n                          ? \"text-green-700\"\n                          : \"text-red-700\"\n                    }`}\n                  >\n                    {fmtPct(totals.distPct)}\n                  </td>\n                  <td className=\"p-2 text-right font-mono\">{fmtMin(totals.fixedDur)}</td>\n                  <td className=\"p-2 text-right font-mono\">{fmtMin(totals.freeDur)}</td>\n                  <td\n                    className={`p-2 text-right font-mono ${\n                      totals.durPct == null\n                        ? \"\"\n                        : totals.durPct >= 0\n                          ? \"text-green-700\"\n                          : \"text-red-700\"\n                    }`}\n                  >\n                    {fmtPct(totals.durPct)}\n                  </td>\n                  <td className=\"p-2\" colSpan={2} />\n                </tr>\n              </tfoot>\n            )}\n          </table>\n          <p className=\"mt-2 text-xs text-gray-500\">\n            Amber rows: fixed and free runs left a different number of stops unassigned, so their\n            distance/duration deltas are not apples-to-apples. Totals include only routes where\n            both runs produced a feasible route.\n          </p>\n        </section>\n      )}\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction RowStatus({ row }: { row: BatchRow }) {\n  if (row.status === \"queued\") {\n    return <span className=\"text-xs px-2 py-0.5 rounded-full bg-gray-100 text-gray-600\">queued</span>;\n  }\n  if (row.status === \"running\") {\n    return <span className=\"text-xs px-2 py-0.5 rounded-full bg-blue-100 text-blue-800\">running…</span>;\n  }\n  if (row.status === \"error\") {\n    return (\n      <span\n        className=\"text-xs px-2 py-0.5 rounded-full bg-red-100 text-red-800\"\n        title={row.error}\n      >\n        error\n      </span>\n    );\n  }\n  if (row.error || row.fixed?.noRoutes || row.free?.noRoutes) {\n    return (\n      <span\n        className=\"text-xs px-2 py-0.5 rounded-full bg-amber-100 text-amber-800\"\n        title={row.error ?? \"one side produced no feasible routes\"}\n      >\n        partial\n      </span>\n    );\n  }\n  return <span className=\"text-xs px-2 py-0.5 rounded-full bg-green-100 text-green-800\">done</span>;\n}\n"
}
```
